clue.text: I live to destroy people: time for a change

parts.note: 'I am' is to say I exist, I live
to end something is to destroy it
men are people
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A misanthrope declares a mission of destruction and announces that the moment for change has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes the first part read as a manifesto, but every word is a building block: 'I live' is AM, as in 'I am', so the whole reads AM + END + MEN + T.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration made to a text or motion, so it is literally a modification.

clue.text: Pyromania's what it is — there's no pay — I'm off

definitions.text: Pyromania's what it is — there's no pay — I'm off

indicators.note: 'off' also means wrong or disordered, so what is left after the removals is scrambled
'there's no' says the letters of the following word are absent from the fodder

parts.note: the word with its 's taken as written, the starting fodder
taken as written, these letters are struck out
taken as written, these letters are struck out too

explanation.surface: An arsonist explains that it is no money-making crime, merely a compulsion, and leaves the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PYROMANIAS, remove P, A, Y and I, M, and the leftover R, O, N, A, S rearrange; the whole clue also describes the crime, an unpaid act of a fire-raiser who then flees.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property, the deed a compulsive fire-raiser commits without any financial motive.

clue.text: Cut up a member on the French pattern

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a Member of Parliament is an MP
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A tailor chops up a limb following a French dress pattern, a gruesome sewing lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a limb but is the parliamentary MP; 'on' just strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to be copied, a sample that others follow, as in setting an example.

clue.text: Departs for the other side

parts.note: surface reading: someone sets out for the far side of a river or border
setter's reading: departing for 'the other side' is a euphemism for death, the passing to the afterlife

explanation.walkthrough: It is also one of the stage directions 9 across refers to: a character who expires on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over to the other side is a gentle euphemism for expiring, leaving life behind.

clue.text: Departs for the unknown, about which there's a drawback

indicators.note: 'back' tells us the word for draw is read from end to start
'about which there's' puts the reversed draw around the unknown

parts.note: the word splits into draw plus back; a draw in a match is a tie
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone heads off into uncharted territory, and the trip has a downside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning a disadvantage, but splits into draw and back. Exit is also a stage direction, one of the examples at 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit is the stage direction for a single actor leaving, meaning he or she goes off.

clue.text: Turn thong with sheath knife provided by 16's creator

parts.note: taken as written, first half of the fodder
taken as written, second half of the fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions for a woodsman: twist a leather strap together with a sheathed blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like the instruction to rearrange but is itself part of the twenty letters; no separate signal is given. 16 is ALICE, whose creator was Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll, who wrote the Alice books, also wrote this nonsense poem about a voyage to catch an imaginary beast.

clue.text: Other ranks left to work on the bottom deck

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
L is the abbreviation for left
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Ordinary sailors are left behind to labour down on the lowest level of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing warship, below the waterline.

clue.text: See 5
It reflects on the family where there's little room for vocal horse girl

parts.note: the loo is the lavatory, often called the little room
kin are one's family

indicators.note: 'vocal' means the following word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, and said aloud it is two letter Gs
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Musings on a cramped family home where there is no space even for a girl's pony.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the little room sits on top of the family. Gee-gee is a nursery word for a horse, and spoken it is two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is an old word for a mirror, which reflects whatever stands before it.

clue.text: Pre-Christmas appeal is nothing to saint entering the gates

indicators.note: 'entering' puts the pieces before it inside the gates

parts.note: the pearly gates are the entrance to heaven, so 'gates' points to pearly
O is zero, nothing
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint arriving at heaven's gates finds the place indifferent to the Christmas rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The gates are those a saint would enter, the pearly gates of heaven; O and ST go in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Post early for Christmas' was the long-running Royal Mail slogan urging people to send cards in good time.

clue.text: Coach gets bearings — 3 and 4 for 2

parts.note: a stagecoach is a coach, shortened to stage
bearings are compass directions

explanation.surface: A trainer takes compass readings before a numbered set of moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down DIES and 4 down EXIT, for 2 down EXAMPLE: they are examples of instructions printed in a play's script.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit and dies are both instructions printed in a playscript telling actors what happens, so they are instances of this category.

clue.text: Primate of the north gets it in the neck

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A northern ape, or a northern archbishop, gets a nasty blow to the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' also means an archbishop, and 'gets it in the neck' is a phrase for being punished; neither sense matters here.
explanation.definitionFit: The nape is the back of the neck, standing for the whole part of the body here.

clue.text: Of course use the gun: it's infallible

parts.note: 'sure' is an informal way of saying of course
to fire is to use a gun

explanation.surface: A gunman is told that shooting is the method that cannot fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surefire is certain to succeed, so it cannot go wrong.

clue.text: The chances are there'll be five in one set

parts.note: a means one
a set of false teeth is dentures
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A gambler says the odds are good that a five will turn up in any one round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a set in tennis or cards, but it is a set of false teeth; V goes in after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are risky undertakings, hazards where you take your chance, so the plural matches 'chances'.

clue.text: Prevailed over the German student with a remarkable situation

parts.note: to prevail is to win
der is a German word for 'the'
L is a learner, a student driver
and means with, in addition to

explanation.surface: A victory over a German student, achieved in a striking set of circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' works because this is a down entry: the first piece sits above the rest. L for learner comes from British L-plates on learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonderland is a marvellous place or state of affairs, and also the scene of Carroll's first Alice book.

clue.text: A Bedfordshire poet fiddled with an outboard

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper with it and so jumble it

parts.note: taken as written
Beds is the standard abbreviation of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rural English versifier tinkers with a boat engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is typically a fast motorboat driven by an outboard motor, so the motorboat is named by its engine.

clue.text: Salt and where it comes from at home with layabout

parts.note: salt comes from the sea

indicators.note: 'with' joined to the 'about' inside layabout wraps the ballad round the phrase for at home

parts.note: the word splits into lay plus about; a lay is a ballad
in means at home

explanation.surface: Salt, its seaside origin and a lazy person lounging around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layabout' looks like an idler but splits into lay plus about, the container signal hidden in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is the most common flavouring added to food, the standard example of a condiment.

clue.text: Francophone part of Anglophone country is the flower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a French-speaking African country whose name is the first part of its English-speaking neighbour's
second meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the great West African one

explanation.surface: A French-speaking region of an English-speaking land has a national bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword slang for a river. The French-speaking country's name is literally part of the name of its English-speaking neighbour Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a former French colony in West Africa and to the major river flowing through it.

clue.text: She had 12 in 13 and penetrated 7 26

parts.note: setter's reading: a girl who had adventures in wonderland, the first book's title
setter's reading: she went through the looking glass, the second book's title

explanation.walkthrough: The numbers fill in from 12 down, 13 down and 7 down/26 across, giving the titles of Lewis Carroll's two books about one girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's heroine stars in Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass, so she is the girl described.

clue.text: It's doing nothing that keeps one going

definitions.meaning: first meaning: idleness, a disinclination to act
second meaning: in physics, the property by which a moving body continues in motion unless a force stops it

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a paradox about idleness giving energy; the two halves are the everyday and the physics senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In daily speech the word means sluggish apathy; in physics it is a body's tendency to stay at rest or keep moving steadily.

clue.text: Inclined to err, upper-class dandy, double drab

wordplay.note: two words each meaning drab: dun, a dull greyish brown, and dreary

explanation.surface: A description of a foppish, blundering aristocrat dressed in doubly dull colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double drab' asks for two synonyms of drab placed side by side: DUN + DREARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Dundreary is the foolish, foppish aristocrat of the play Our American Cousin, a byword for a muddle-headed swell.

clue.text: Give the job and order some beer outside

indicators.note: 'outside' puts the beer around the word for order

parts.note: a pint is some beer
PO is a postal order

explanation.surface: Hire someone and then buy a round of drinks outside the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PO goes inside A PINT, after its P. A postal order is a British money order bought at a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to assign them to a post, placing them in a position.

clue.text: It's obvious the vessel will capsize

parts.note: overt means open, obvious
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Anyone can see the ship is about to roll over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which fits capsizing, but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to turn upside down, just as a boat does when it tips over.

clue.text: Composition for the voice addressed to cat

indicators.note: 'for the voice' means what follows is spoken, so we go by sound

parts.note: the old vocative way to call to a cat: O plus the pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A song written for a singer, dedicated to a pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition for the voice' looks like the definition, a song; only 'Composition' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for work and is used for a numbered musical piece by a composer.

clue.text: The upshot is, bonnie 14ac's destination's right

parts.note: the Skye Boat Song runs 'Speed, bonnie boat ... over the sea to Skye', the Scottish island
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The conclusion reached: the bonnie boat's goal is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across is SPEEDBOAT, and 'Speed, bonnie boat' opens the Skye Boat Song. 'Upshot' reads as a result but is literally a shot hit upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a skyer is a ball hit high into the air, quite literally a shot that goes up.

clue.text: See 24
Model in a funny picture

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'in' places the model inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: quaint means odd, funny
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An artist's sitter appears in a comic painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a sitter for a painting but is Ford's Model T, giving just the T, which goes after A QUA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquatint is an etching made by a process that imitates watercolour washes, and so a kind of print or image.

clue.text: Exposed tiny quarrel in Northern Ireland — lest one should suspect a cover-up?

definitions.text: lest one should suspect a cover-up?

indicators.note: something exposed is laid open and pulled apart, so these letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A small dispute in Northern Ireland is made public to head off any accusation of hushing things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a cryptic definition: an organisation investigates itself to show it hides nothing, though the irony is it may itself be a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation holds an investigation into its own conduct, ostensibly to show the public it is concealing nothing.

clue.text: See 7 Down
Dese days it pulls de plough — can't I let well alone?

definitions.text: Dese days it pulls de plough
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the dialect of the clue, 'de' is 'the', and nowadays a tractor pulls the plough
second meaning: someone who keeps finding fault even when things are fine

explanation.surface: A rustic voice laments modern farm machinery and asks why it cannot leave a good thing be.
explanation.walkthrough: The dialect spelling 'de' for 'the' is the hint: say 'de tractor' and you have the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who disparages things can never leave well enough alone, always running down what is already good.
